notes:
kb/Work PB352. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 1): 'The access mode of the file referenced by file-name-1 shall be either sequential or dynamic.' CODE: BindStart -- if (file.AccessMode == FileAccessMode.Random) ctx.Edition.Error('COBOL0862', ... 'the access mode shall be sequential or dynamic (ISO 14.9.41 SR1)'). FileAccessMode is {Sequential, Random, Dynamic}, so the single Random test is the exact complement of the rule's permitted pair, and FileModel.AccessMode DEFAULTS to Sequential -- a SELECT with no ACCESS clause (the implicit arm a check written against an explicit clause would miss) does not false-fire. ctx.Edition.Error is unconditional, so the diagnostic fires at every strictness and every edition, right for a rule with no edition delta.
PROBED on BOTH keyed organizations, because the check sits before the organization split and a one-organization probe would not have shown that: indexed ACCESS RANDOM (out-b1/probe/sr1-sr8) and relative ACCESS RANDOM (out-b1/probe/sr1-rel) each report COBOL0862 SR1.
ONE EDGE NOT REACHED, and it is benign: the check sits AFTER 'if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported(...)', so a sequential-organization file never reaches SR1. 12.4.5.2 admits only ACCESS SEQUENTIAL for sequential organization, so no conforming program can exercise that arm -- the hole is in the diagnostic for an already-illegal file control entry, and 12.4.5.2 owns it, not this rule.
TEST: NONE. grep for COBOL0862 across tests/ returns zero hits -- no negative fixture, no unit test -- so a green suite proves nothing about this row. conformance:cases/12.4.5.7-COLLATING-SEQUENCE/file_collating_seq exercises only the ACCEPT side (ACCESS DYNAMIC) and would still pass with this check deleted. Closing needs a negative fixture pinning COBOL0862 on ORGANIZATION INDEXED + ACCESS RANDOM + START, and its relative twin. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The adjudicator's own note names an unreached edge -- the SR1 check sits AFTER 'if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported(...)' at KeyedIoBinder.cs:208, so a sequential-organization file never reaches it -- and then argues the edge away with a premise I MEASURED AND BROKE: 'no conforming program can exercise that arm ... 12.4.5.2 owns it, not this rule'. The premise is half right and the conclusion is wrong. Half right: I read the file control entry general formats (specs/ISO_COBOL.md 12.4.5.1) rather than trusting the paraphrase, and Format 3 (sequential) does carry only '[ ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL ]' -- ACCESS RANDOM on a sequential file is indeed not conforming. Wrong: nothing in this compiler diagnoses it. ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL + ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM + START SQF FIRST compiles CLEAN -- exit 0, prb.dll written, ZERO diagnostics -- so the rule that was supposed to own the hole owns nothing, and a program that violates SR1 ('the access mode of the file referenced by file-name-1 shall be either sequential or dynamic') is accepted in silence and becomes NotImplemented.Run at run time. SR1 is therefore enforced over two of the three organizations START can name and unenforced over the third; that is PARTIAL by the stated burden (an unverified edge => PARTIAL, and this one is worse than unverified -- it is verified to miss). I did NOT charge SR1 with the sequential-file rejection itself: that mechanism is already recorded as DIVERGES on SR-14.9.41.3-2, and if it is fixed the SR1 test, sitting below it, would start covering sequential files unchanged. What I charge is the CONFORMS claim, whose sole justification for the uncovered half was an escape hatch that does not exist. Everything else in the record I re-derived and it held: FileModel.cs:10 'enum FileAccessMode { Sequential, Random, Dynamic }' makes the single Random test the exact complement of the rule's permitted pair; FileModel.cs:54 'AccessMode { get; set; } = FileAccessMode.Sequential' makes the implicit arm safe; EditionContext.cs:109 'Error(...) => Diagnostics.Add($"{Prefix()}error {code}...")' is unconditional. Citation re-run and OK. Test-ref is empty, which is expected and not what moved the verdict.

LANDED 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB352).
